Dental implants are one of the most trusted and effective solutions for replacing missing teeth. At Nash Dental Group, we take pride in offering state-of-the-art implant dentistry designed to restore both the function and beauty of your smile. Implants are small titanium posts that act as artificial tooth roots, providing a secure and stable foundation for crowns, bridges, or dentures.

Unlike traditional dentures, dental implants fuse with your jawbone, helping to prevent bone loss and preserve your facial structure. They look, feel, and function like natural teeth—allowing you to speak, chew, and smile with confidence.

Our team provides a comprehensive implant experience, starting with a personalized consultation and digital imaging to carefully plan your treatment. From surgical placement to final restoration, every step is completed with precision and care. We focus on patient comfort, long-term results, and making the process as smooth and stress-free as possible.

Dental implants are titanium posts placed into the jawbone to replace missing tooth roots. They provide a strong base for crowns, bridges, or dentures and offer a permanent alternative to traditional tooth replacement options.

[/et_pb_blurb][et_pb_blurb title=”Why should I choose implants over dentures or bridges?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Noto Serif Display|700|||||||” header_font_size=”30px” body_font=”Nunito||||||||” body_font_size=”18px” body_line_height=”1.4em” header_text_align_tablet=”” header_text_align_phone=”center” header_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” body_text_align_tablet=”” body_text_align_phone=”center” body_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Implants are more stable, natural-looking, and long-lasting. They prevent jawbone deterioration and don’t require altering adjacent teeth, unlike some bridge procedures.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column][et_pb_column type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.22.1″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_blurb title=”What exactly are dental implants?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Noto Serif Display|700|||||||” header_font_size=”30px” body_font=”Nunito||||||||” body_font_size=”18px” body_line_height=”1.4em” header_text_align_tablet=”” header_text_align_phone=”center” header_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” body_text_align_tablet=”” body_text_align_phone=”center” body_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

With proper oral hygiene and routine dental visits, implants can last a lifetime. The crown or restoration attached to the implant may eventually need replacement, but the implant itself is built to endure for decades.

[/et_pb_blurb][et_pb_blurb title=”How long does the treatment process take?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Noto Serif Display|700|||||||” header_font_size=”30px” body_font=”Nunito||||||||” body_font_size=”18px” body_line_height=”1.4em” header_text_align_tablet=”” header_text_align_phone=”center” header_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” body_text_align_tablet=”” body_text_align_phone=”center” body_text_align_last_edited=”on|phone” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

The process typically takes a few months, allowing time for the implant to fuse with the jawbone (a process called osseointegration). The exact timeline varies for each patient.
